original_question: Given a positive distance d and a plane figure or space body, determine the maximum size of a set of points with pairwise distances at least d, determine the minimum size of a set of points that d-covers the figure in the sense that every added point lies within distance d of one of the chosen points, and study the corresponding variants for interior points only, boundary points only, or strict inequalities.
target_in_paper: The draft is closest to the general "More generally: let d > 0" formulation in Unsolved Problem 33, parts (a)–(c), on p. 28, not to the opening special-case question about a parallelogram/prism. Problem 33 explicitly restates the separation and covering questions and then adds the interior/frontier and inequality variants; it also clearly extends the earlier Unsolved Problem 2 on p. 6. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the two main extremal questions in the paper’s general formulation: maximizing the size of a d-separated set of points in a plane figure or space body, and minimizing the size of a point set that covers the figure/body at radius d. It also correctly notices that the paper asks for location-restricted and inequality-modified variants. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is Unsolved Problem 33’s generalization on p. 28, not merely Unsolved Problem 2; Problem 33 is the place where the variants you mention are explicitly listed. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The paper keeps the setting narrow: a given plane figure in the plane, or, in the spatial version, a given space body; it does not formulate the problem for arbitrary metric spaces or arbitrary dimensions. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Part (c) distinguishes three separate location regimes: only interior points, interior and frontier points together, and frontier points only. Your draft mentions interior-only and boundary-only, but omits the explicit middle regime. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The covering side should be quantified directly over all points of the figure/body: for every point A in the figure/body, one of the chosen points Ai must satisfy the stated distance condition. The paper does not use the term "d-cover". ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The inequality variants should be stated exactly rather than as a generic reference to "strict inequalities": Problem 33(c) separately singles out the strict separation condition and a corresponding covering-condition variant. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

There is an OCR-level ambiguity in the PDF: part (b) and item (5) both appear as "AAi < d," which would make item (5) redundant. So a stand-alone rewrite should either preserve the paper’s wording with a note of ambiguity, or normalize the covering clause so that the listed strict variant remains meaningful. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Problem 33 begins with a specific solved case about interior points in a parallelogram with angle π/3 and the analogous prism; your draft does not include that special case, so the refined question should be anchored to the subsequent general open problem only. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
The paper explicitly says that these generalized questions are open in general, aside from particular cases. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let F ⊂ R^2 be a given plane figure and, in the spatial version, let K ⊂ R^3 be a given space body. For a fixed real number d > 0, determine (i) the maximum cardinality of a subset S ⊂ F (respectively S ⊂ K) such that the Euclidean distance between any two distinct points of S is at least d, and (ii) the minimum cardinality of a subset C = {A1, A2, ...} ⊂ F (respectively ⊂ K) such that every point A of F (respectively K) lies within distance d of some Ai. Study exactly the additional variants listed in the paper: the versions using only interior points, using interior together with frontier points, using frontier points only, and the strict-inequality versions obtained by replacing the separation condition by |PQ| > d and, on the covering side, by the corresponding strict covering inequality. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the special parallelogram/prism calculation at the start of Unsolved Problem 33, but at the immediately following generalization. That generalization reproduces the older Unsolved Problem 2 and adds precisely the interior/frontier and inequality variants that appear in your draft. Solution (III) then states that these generalized versions are open in general. In the refined question I made the Euclidean ambient spaces explicit and converted the paper’s prose into quantified set language so that the question stands alone. On the covering side, I used the neutral/base phrase "within distance d" and then the strict covering variant, because the OCR prints "< d" both in part (b) and in item (5); treating item (5) as the strict version is an inference from the internal structure of part (c), where item (4) is the strict variant for part (a). ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
